findings.title: Mobile startup imports depend on undeclared workspace packages
findings.trigger: Install dependencies in a fresh checkout and bundle the /chat route.
findings.impact: The chat startup graph imports groups-config, personas-generator, memory-scope, speech-cloud and media packages that the mobile manifest does not declare. Local manually created node_modules junctions are not reproduced by a clean install, so bundling can fail before the app opens.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/composition/chat/screen.tsx imports groups-config at line 50 and personas-generator at line 119; persona-memory.ts imports memory-scope; voice/container.ts imports speech-cloud; composition/media/providers.ts imports media-engine and media-integration. These packages are absent from apps/mobile/package.json and the lockfile importers. Existing local links are Windows junctions.
findings.fix: Declare every runtime workspace dependency in its consuming package and regenerate the pinned pnpm lockfile.
findings.verification: Confirmed by source and dependency-manifest inspection; clean install/bundle not executed.

findings.title: Sync core packages are excluded from the workspace
findings.trigger: Resolve @locallab/sync-merge, sync-transport or sync-composition through a clean pnpm workspace install.
findings.impact: The new packages live at packages/sync/core/*, one directory deeper than packages/*/*. No matching workspace glob exists. The in-progress sync-icloud package already declares sync-merge as workspace:*, making dependency resolution fail on a clean install.
findings.evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml includes packages/*, packages/*/*, packages/chat/engine/* and other explicit deep patterns but no packages/sync/core/*. packages/sync/icloud/package.json declares @locallab/sync-merge: workspace:*.
findings.fix: Add packages/sync/core/* to the workspace and regenerate the lockfile.
findings.verification: Confirmed by path and manifest inspection; installer not executed. T100 is in-progress code, not a completed-task regression claim.

findings.title: Saving a group deadlocks the app database queue
findings.trigger: Save a valid room from GroupSetupPanel using the app's sharedMobileDatabase connection.
findings.impact: dbTransaction awaits a transaction callback that issues writes through the outer this.db. The outer adapter queues those writes behind the transaction that is waiting for them. The transaction never commits and every later database operation, including chat sends, waits indefinitely.
findings.evidence: saveRoom calls dbTransaction(this.db, async () => ...) and uses this.db.runAsync inside the callback. dbTransaction passes work directly to withTransactionAsync without exposing its transaction argument. apps/mobile/platform/database.ts queues outer operations and supplies a separate transaction-scoped port.
findings.fix: Pass the supplied transaction port into the callback and perform every room and participant write on that port.
findings.verification: Confirmed by source control-flow inspection; runtime reproduction not executed.

findings.title: Resetting Persona memory scope deadlocks the app database
findings.trigger: Call SQLitePersonaMemoryScope.resetPersona on the shared mobile database.
findings.impact: The transaction callback awaits this.db.runAsync on the outer queue instead of the supplied transaction connection. Its writes wait for the transaction to finish while the transaction waits for its writes, permanently blocking the shared database queue.
findings.evidence: resetPersona calls this.db.withTransactionAsync(async () => ...) and both DELETE statements use this.db. The shared database adapter queues external operations after the active transaction.
findings.fix: Accept the transaction callback parameter and use that scoped port for both DELETE statements.
findings.verification: Confirmed by source control-flow inspection. No current mobile UI caller was found; this is a blocker in the package reset API, not an observed UI freeze. Runtime reproduction not executed.

findings.title: Voice Studio reads a nonexistent audio_uri column
findings.trigger: Create a fresh SQLiteTranscriptionImportStore and call list(), including on normal chat-screen initialization.
findings.impact: The SELECT fails with no such column: audio_uri. The Promise.all that also loads Personas and cloud voice connections rejects and silently leaves all three lists empty, disabling imported recording playback and Persona cloud voice selection.
findings.evidence: ensureSchema creates audio_path at line 34; add writes audio_path; list selects audio_uri AS audioUri. apps/mobile/composition/chat/screen.tsx:861 groups imports, Personas and connection loading in one Promise.all followed by an empty catch.
findings.fix: Select audio_path AS audioUri and avoid letting one optional list failure suppress the other lists.
findings.verification: Confirmed schema/query contradiction; SQL execution not run.

findings.title: Initial copy tombstones the source records it must retain
findings.trigger: Choose copy-phone or copy-mac when both stores share entity IDs, or let the source deliver before the target calls runInitialSync.
findings.impact: replaceLocalSet tombstones every live target row with a new wall-clock revision. Source rows retain their older revisions, so shared IDs cannot be restored; source-first delivery is deleted after receipt. Initial sync is then marked done with missing conversations/messages.
findings.evidence: runInitialSync separately sends liveSourceRecords or calls replaceLocalSet. replaceLocalSet deletes every live snapshot entry without a source membership set. envelope preserves old revisions, and MergeStore suppresses records older than existing tombstones. Existing copy fixtures run target first and use disjoint IDs.
findings.fix: Coordinate the copy using a source snapshot/membership manifest and atomically replace the target with those members, deleting only rows absent from the source.
findings.verification: Confirmed by source ordering and merge rules; adversarial scenario not executed.

findings.title: Recreating a saved pairing reuses encryption keys and nonces
findings.trigger: Create two client instances from the same saved QR, such as before and after an app restart, and send the first frame from each.
findings.impact: The same pairing secret and route derive the same salts, keys and sequence-zero nonce. Reusing an AES-GCM nonce compromises sealed-frame security, while a peer retaining its replay state refuses the restarted client.
findings.evidence: deriveSessionSalts is deterministic per QR secret and route. createPairingClient constructs fresh createSessionPairing channels each time. SealingChannel initializes nextSequence to 0 in packages/remote/crypto/src/index.ts:192.
findings.fix: Negotiate fresh session material on reconnect before resetting counters, or persist a safe nonce space and peer replay state across restarts.
findings.verification: Confirmed by deterministic key/nonce construction; cryptographic runtime probe not executed.

findings.title: Asynchronous acknowledgements leave later sync batches unsent
findings.trigger: Enqueue 600 valid records, let sendBatch resolve before the WebSocket acknowledgement arrives, then deliver the acknowledgement for the first 500.
findings.impact: sendPending returns after the first unacknowledged send. onFrame handles the acknowledgement and returns without pumping the remaining batch. No acknowledgement timer is scheduled. The remaining 100 rows stay pending indefinitely and initialSyncDone may already be recorded.
findings.evidence: transport/src/index.ts:167 returns when head is not yet acknowledged; composition/src/index.ts:190 calls handleAck and immediately returns; neither implementation schedules acknowledgement retries. The 600-record fixture invokes handleAck inside send, hiding asynchronous delivery.
findings.fix: Pump the next batch after an acknowledgement and schedule a bounded acknowledgement timeout/retry without overlapping send pumps.
findings.verification: Confirmed by source control flow and fixture structure; real WebSocket scenario not executed.

findings.title: Mac MLX worker blocks its own inference tasks while reading stdin
findings.trigger: Keep the worker stdin open and send a load or generate command, then wait for a result.
findings.impact: Worker.run is MainActor-isolated and calls synchronous readLine in a loop without suspending. The load/generation Task closures inherit that actor and cannot execute while the loop blocks waiting for another line. Normal persistent-worker inference never begins.
findings.evidence: The Worker class is annotated @MainActor. run contains while let line = readLine(). The load/unload/generate cases create Task closures but do not await or yield. Both runtime work and completion events are inside those closures.
findings.fix: Read stdin on a dedicated blocking thread or feed commands through an asynchronous stream so the actor can execute generation and cancellation tasks.
findings.verification: Confirmed actor/control-flow defect by source inspection; Mac worker not executed.

findings.title: Native download pause method has an incompatible Swift return type
findings.trigger: Compile BackgroundTransferSession.swift into the native downloader.
findings.impact: pause is declared to return Data?, but its checked continuation resumes with data?.base64EncodedString(), which is String?. The native implementation cannot type-check as written, blocking the background downloader build.
findings.evidence: The declaration at line 79 is async throws -> Data?. Line 84 passes the optional base64 String to continuation.resume(returning:). The TypeScript bridge expects resumeData as a string.
findings.fix: Make the Swift return type String? to match the bridge, or return Data and perform encoding in a correctly typed bridge layer.
findings.verification: Confirmed static type contradiction; Swift compilation not available/executed on this Windows review host.

findings.title: Cloud adapters discard the tool results required by the next tool round
findings.trigger: Run a registered tool such as current_time or web_search with Anthropic, OpenAI advanced, Gemini or Mistral and start the following model round.
findings.impact: The app uses ToolLoopEngine's canonical assistant/tool exchange, but these provider encoders discard every kind=tool entry instead of translating its result. Several also omit the assistant tool-call structure. The model never receives the tool output, so autonomous tool requests cannot reliably reach a grounded final reply and may repeat until the loop limit.
findings.evidence: appendToolExchange creates kind=tool rows in packages/tools/engine/src/index.ts:743. Mobile constructs ToolLoopEngine without appendExchange at screen.tsx:1754. Anthropic encoder accepts only user/assistant after system handling; OpenAI advanced line 50, Gemini line 304 and Mistral line 316 likewise filter out tool. No provider-specific replay mapper is supplied by composition.
findings.fix: Implement vendor-specific tool call/result replay in each affected adapter or supply a matching appendExchange mapper; preserve native call IDs and required reasoning blocks where applicable.
findings.verification: Confirmed by tracing canonical exchange into source encoders; live provider rounds not executed.
findings.owner: Provider encoders and T070 tool integration

findings.title: Hugging Face enqueue API rejects its declared revision argument
findings.trigger: Call ModelLifecycleRegistry.enqueueHuggingFace with any string revision as required by its public TypeScript signature.
findings.impact: RevisionSchema requires a strict object containing wallMs, counter and deviceId, so every correctly typed string argument throws before jobs.create. The package's Hugging Face enqueue path is unusable to typed consumers.
findings.evidence: enqueueHuggingFace declares revision: string at line 253 and then calls RevisionSchema.parse(revision) at line 260. The contract in packages/contracts/src/identity.ts requires an object. Existing descriptor tests never call enqueueHuggingFace.
findings.fix: Type the argument as Revision and pass that validated object to JobStore.create, or explicitly parse a serialized revision before validation if serialization is the intended API.
findings.verification: Confirmed signature/schema contradiction; method not executed and mobile Hugging Face UI is not currently mounted.

findings.title: Legacy MCP SSE transport waits for replies on the wrong channel
findings.trigger: Connect to a legacy HTTP+SSE MCP server whose POST accepts messages and whose GET stream delivers JSON-RPC replies.
findings.impact: Initialization POST acceptance is parsed as if it contained a JSON-RPC response. The legacy GET stream is no longer consumed after the endpoint event. Initialization fails or waits until timeout; no tools from compliant legacy servers are available.
findings.evidence: discoverLegacySse stops iterating frames after the endpoint event at line 616 and calls postRpc for initialize at line 641. postRpc passes the POST response to readEnvelope. No persistent GET-stream response dispatcher exists. Legacy specification requires server replies as SSE message events: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2024-11-05/basic/transports
findings.fix: Keep the legacy GET stream active for the session and dispatch SSE message replies by JSON-RPC ID; treat POST responses as message acceptance.
findings.verification: Confirmed by source tracing against the primary legacy MCP specification; live server reproduction not executed.

findings.title: MCP SSE parser never recognizes CRLF message boundaries
findings.trigger: Receive an MCP SSE response framed with CRLF lines and CRLF blank lines, such as data: {...} followed by two CRLF sequences.
findings.impact: The parser searches the unnormalized buffer for LF-LF. CRLF-CRLF does not contain that sequence, so no frame is yielded. Initialization or tool calls hang until their timeout; without a timeout the retained buffer can grow indefinitely.
findings.evidence: readEventStreamFrames searches buffer.indexOf("\n\n") before normalizing CRLF in the extracted frame. Thus valid CRLF streams never reach the normalization or JSON-RPC parser.
findings.fix: Normalize line endings incrementally, including split CRLF across chunks, before detecting blank lines; bound retained frame bytes and cancel the owned reader on exit.
findings.verification: Confirmed by literal delimiter/control-flow inspection; live stream execution not performed.

findings.title: MCP discovery escapes the chat setup deadline and can lock sending indefinitely
findings.trigger: Enable an MCP server that successfully initializes, then leaves its tools/list response open without replying.
findings.impact: collectMcpTools passes the 15-second chat deadline only to initialize. createMcpTools replaces it with a fresh never-aborted signal, and the client has no configured timeout. Chat remains awaiting discovery with sendPending=true and working=true, preventing subsequent sends or mode changes until restart.
findings.evidence: createMcpTools creates new AbortController().signal and awaits discoverTools with it. collectMcpTools creates a client without timeoutMs and awaits createMcpTools after initialize. screen.tsx:1678 creates a 15-second controller but awaits collectMcpTools before starting the run; its finally releases send admission only after that await settles.
findings.fix: Accept and propagate the caller AbortSignal through createMcpTools/discoverTools and apply one bounded setup deadline to every discovery request; ensure deadline cleanup runs in finally.
findings.verification: Confirmed by source cancellation/data-flow tracing; stalled-server reproduction not executed.
findings.owner: MCP client and mobile tool collection

findings.title: Initial Persona photo sync rejects the batch before its Persona arrives
findings.trigger: Perform initial merge/copy sync from a source with a selected Persona and its selected photo to a receiver that has neither row.
findings.impact: Source snapshots sort attachment records before persona records. The receiver photo gate requires an existing local Persona reference, so it rejects the first attachment before applying the Persona later in the same batch. No acknowledgement is sent; retrying the unchanged batch cannot converge and also blocks following chat records.
findings.evidence: MergeStore.snapshot sorts entityType/entityId keys; liveSourceRecords preserves that order. onFrame admits and applies one record at a time, throwing before acknowledgement. personaTierGate attachment admission only uses ctx.attachmentOwner, which is a local lookup. No pending-batch ownership preflight or dependency ordering exists.
findings.fix: Validate selected incoming Persona ownership for the full batch before applying photo records, or order/admit dependencies explicitly while preserving privacy checks and transactional acknowledgement semantics.
findings.verification: Confirmed by source ordering and admission tracing; two-device execution not performed.
findings.owner: T099 Persona sync admission and T098 composition

findings.title: Autolinked iOS speech module contains Swift compilation errors
findings.trigger: Build the iOS mobile app with its declared @locallab/speech-system dependency autolinked.
findings.impact: The PCM capture branch calls throwing AVAudioEngine.start without try. The AVAudioConverter input block also writes .pointee on its first argument (packet count) instead of the second argument (input-status pointer). The speech native target cannot compile, blocking the iOS app build.
findings.evidence: startCapture line 343 calls engine.start() while the same file correctly uses try self.engine!.start() in dictation. Conversion block lines 329-335 names arguments status,outCondition but assigns status.pointee. apps/mobile/package.json declares speech-system and its Expo module config registers the Swift class.
findings.fix: Call try engine.start() and update outCondition.pointee in the conversion input block; compile the autolinked target on macOS before claiming native completion.
findings.verification: Confirmed source type/call contradictions; Swift/iOS compilation not executed on this Windows host.

findings.title: ComfyUI rejects successful prompt submissions with empty node_errors
findings.trigger: Submit a valid graph to a normal ComfyUI /prompt endpoint returning {prompt_id,number,node_errors:{}}.
findings.impact: The empty object is truthy, so the adapter throws malformed before recording prompt_id or following outputs. Every successful submission is reported failed while the server may still generate the image; retries can submit additional unwanted work.
findings.evidence: run checks if (promptRecord.node_errors) and throws. The official server successful branch queues the prompt and returns node_errors: valid[3], an object: https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/blob/master/server.py . Fixtures omitting this field do not model this response.
findings.fix: Distinguish actual prompt rejection/error from an empty diagnostics map and retain prompt_id for every accepted submission.
findings.verification: Source tracing against official ComfyUI server; real backend execution not performed.

findings.title: Applying LoRA rewires the default graph VAE to a CLIP output
findings.trigger: Build the default ComfyUI graph with at least one selected LoRA.
findings.impact: VAEDecode.vae originally points to CheckpointLoaderSimple output 2. applyLoras replaces every nonzero checkpoint output with the final LoRA CLIP output 1. The resulting graph supplies CLIP where VAE is required and the server rejects it; default LoRA generation is unusable.
findings.evidence: defaultGraph node 6 uses vae:["1",2]. applyLoras rewrites all checkpoint references with value[1]===0 ? modelSource : clipSource, so output 2 is corrupted. LoRA loaders only replace MODEL and CLIP, not the unchanged VAE.
findings.fix: Rewrite only output slots 0 and 1; preserve VAE and any other checkpoint outputs. Allocate collision-free LoRA node IDs for imported graphs.
findings.verification: Confirmed by source graph transformation; server execution not performed.

findings.title: Relay Docker deployment cannot install the pnpm workspace
findings.trigger: Run the documented repository-root Docker build or docker-compose.relay.yml build.
findings.impact: The image runs npm ci although no package-lock exists. Installation fails before the relay can start. The root also has no npm workspace configuration, so merely supplying a lock would not link the copied workspace:* relay dependencies.
findings.evidence: Dockerfile copies package.json/package-lock.json* and runs npm ci --omit=dev. The current root has pnpm-lock.yaml and packageManager pnpm@8.15.9, no package-lock.json, and workspace membership is declared in pnpm-workspace.yaml rather than root npm workspaces.
findings.fix: Build/install with the pinned pnpm workspace and lockfile, or produce an explicit deployable package bundle with resolved workspace dependencies.
findings.verification: Confirmed build inputs and install-command mismatch; Docker build not executed.

findings.title: Out-of-order encrypted frames remain replayable after acceptance
findings.trigger: Deliver authentic frame sequence 1 before sequence 0, then resend sequence 0 repeatedly while it remains inside the replay window.
findings.impact: Every repeat of sequence 0 is accepted and decrypted because the older-sequence branch never marks that position seen. The identical Rust receiver has the same defect. A relay that reorders/replays captured valid requests can repeatedly deliver authenticated payloads despite the promised replay protection.
findings.evidence: OpeningChannel.acceptSequence checks the bit for back but returns without setting it. Rust accept_sequence likewise returns Ok without updating seen_mask. Only new high-water sequences set a bit. Authentication also occurs after replay-state mutation.
findings.fix: Commit the corresponding seen bit for every accepted sequence after successful authentication; keep failed authentication from consuming replay state. Apply the same algorithm in both languages.
findings.verification: Confirmed source replay-state transition; live paired execution not performed.

findings.title: iCloud upload completion can discard newer pending edits
findings.trigger: Start publishing revision A; while saveRecords is awaiting the cloud, call noteLocalChange with newer revision B of the same entity; then let A finish.
findings.impact: Completion deletes the pending entry by entity key, removing B even though only A reached the cloud. B is also already in seen, so re-notifying the same change will not enqueue it again. Fetch similarly deletes pending changes for superseded incoming records. Newer local edits can be permanently omitted from sync.
findings.evidence: publish snapshots chunk, awaits saveRecords, then unconditionally pending.delete(entityType:entityId). noteLocalChange can overwrite that key during the await. seen is set at enqueue. fetch treats superseded as crossed and deletes by recordName without comparing the pending revision.
findings.fix: Remove a pending upload only if it still has the exact uploaded revision; retain newer local changes when applying stale cloud records. Serialize passes and persist pending identities for restart recovery.
findings.verification: Confirmed async state transition by source inspection. T100 is in-progress shared code; no native CloudKit bridge/runtime was executed.

findings.title: Acknowledgements of old sync records suppress later updates with the same identity
findings.trigger: Send and acknowledge record ID X, then enqueue a changed or deleted entity using record ID X with a newer revision.
findings.impact: ackedIds retains X forever. The next batch is immediately considered fully acknowledged and removed without sending. Stable record IDs are deliberately reused by initial snapshot replay, and tombstones commonly use the entity ID. Reusing an acknowledged identity silently drops subsequent changes.
findings.evidence: handleAck adds IDs to an unbounded set and never removes them. isFullyAcked checks record.id only, independent of revision/batch. sendPending shifts a fully acknowledged head before calling send. Sync composition envelopes reuse row.recordId and replacement tombstones use entityId.
findings.fix: Scope acknowledgements to a unique change/batch identity or revision, clear completed-window state safely, and reject stale acknowledgements from earlier batches.
findings.verification: Confirmed queue/ack state-machine defect by source inspection; live transport not executed.
